workers.title: Design fix for H2 sync generation
workers.assignment:
Read Docs/clanker/WorkerBrief.md first. UE is reinstalling and no C++ compiler is present, so this is a design task: write the fix as a document, do not attempt a build.

An audit found defect H2 in Source/TheWood/Private/WoodWorldStreaming.cpp:22 - `EnsureTerrainAround` calls `WoodPrepareChunk` synchronously on the game thread with Details=false, costing roughly 21,000 heavy samples per chunk (a 65x65 heightfield plus four World.sample() calls per vertex for finite-difference normals), on every chunk-boundary crossing and once at BeginPlay. Docs/Status.md claims "Runtime object realization stays separate from background value generation", which this contradicts.

Related: H3 (the background job recomputes mesh attributes that line 49 then discards) and M1 (a deep copy of the whole placement-profile table inside the per-coordinate scheduling loop, paid per frame).

Write Docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-07-streaming-h2-h3-fix.md proposing a concrete fix: what moves to the background task, what must stay on the game thread and why, how the terrain-under-player protection is preserved without a synchronous generate, and how H3's wasted work is avoided. Respect the existing metres-core/centimetres-adapter boundary and the determinism requirement. Cite file:line. Write that one file; do not modify source.

workers.title: Design fix for H4 crash loop
workers.assignment:
Read Docs/clanker/WorkerBrief.md first. UE is reinstalling and no C++ compiler is present: design task, write a document, do not attempt a build.

An audit found defect H4 in Source/TheWood/Private/WoodWorldStreaming.cpp:63. `Runtime->Jobs[Key].Get()` is called BEFORE `Runtime->Jobs.Remove(Key)`. If the background task throws, the exception escapes Get(), propagates out of Stream() and out of AWoodWorld::Tick, and the key is never removed from Runtime->Jobs. Every later tick re-selects the same never-removed entry, re-throws and crashes again - a permanent crash loop that also leaves both job slots permanently occupied. There is no try/catch anywhere in WoodWorldStreaming.cpp.

The trigger is reachable because two layers disagree on the legal coordinate range: WoodStreaming.cpp:18-19 only rejects chunk indices beyond INT_MAX minus the retain radius, while WoodGeneration.cpp:151-152 rejects coordinates beyond 999000 metres (about chunk index 7804) by throwing std::invalid_argument from inside the background task.

Write Docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-07-streaming-h4-fix.md covering: the exception-safety fix and why the Remove must precede or accompany the Get, where error isolation belongs so a single bad chunk cannot kill Tick, and how the streaming layer should be made aware of the generator's real coordinate limit so it stops enqueueing work guaranteed to throw. Consider M2's related finding that there is no cancellation path for queued work. Cite file:line. Write that one file; do not modify source.
